title: Standings may double-count matches across overlapping Brasileirão datasets
evidence: analysis.py:212 standings() iterates all sd.matches with _competition_filter('brasileirao') mapping to ['brasileirão','brasileirao (histórico)','serie a']; Brasileirao_Matches.csv (2012-2022), novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (2003-2019, label 'Brasileirão (Histórico)') and BR-Football Serie A rows overlap for 2012-2019, so points/played can be inflated by counting the same fixture twice
suggestion: Restrict standings to a single canonical Brasileirão source per season, or de-duplicate fixtures by (season,date,home,away) before aggregating

title: Aggregate stats over 'all' competitions mix duplicated overlapping fixtures
evidence: analysis.py:298 avg_goals() with no competition filter sums every row in sd.matches; the overlapping Brasileirão/Serie A datasets mean some fixtures are counted more than once, slightly skewing avg_goals_per_match and win-rate splits
suggestion: Deduplicate matches at load time, or document that cross-dataset overlap is expected

title: MCP server tool surface is only unit-tested via analysis, not via a live MCP session
evidence: server.py:31 comment states 'server module itself is a thin adapter'; tests/test_server.py exercises tool callables directly but never starts mcp.run()/stdio transport, so protocol wiring is unverified
suggestion: Add a smoke test that lists tools via the MCP client or asserts FastMCP registration metadata beyond name presence

title: Strong coverage and clean structure
evidence: scores.json test_coverage=0.95; 52 tests across 4 files (test_analysis 23, test_data_loader 13, test_normalizer 11, test_server 5), 0 skips; clear module split analysis/data_loader/normalizer/server
